headline: Red Wings' Dylan Larkin has 'had enough,' won't play as trade stalemate continues
take:
The Athletic reports that Dylan Larkin "had enough" and won't play while the trade stalemate continues, and that the Red Wings have suspended him without pay as he waits for a deal. The Hockey News adds that Detroit released a statement saying it is disappointed by his decision and will keep looking for a trade partner that meets both sides' demands.

On the ice, Larkin's season has been quiet. He has 2 goals and 4 assists in 10 games so far this season, and his own expected goals (the quality of his shots and chances) is 3.03, so he's about one goal short of what those chances should have produced. Last year he scored 34 goals in 74 games. Detroit is 7-5-3 and holds 53% of the expected goals overall, 55% at 5-on-5, and the team's share improves by about 1.4 points when he's on the ice. That's a modest gain, but it suggests this is a team that creates more than it allows, and losing a 21.7-minute-a-night forward costs real depth. For fantasy, he's stashed in limbo until a trade lands.
